title: What Scripture Says of Heaven
key_points: Heaven is the Father's house, a prepared place for a prepared people.
The Lord Jesus Christ promised the dying thief he would be with Him in paradise that same day.
What makes Heaven Heaven is the presence of God Himself, not streets or gates.
God will wipe away every tear, and Heaven exceeds anything the heart of man has imagined.

verse.text: Let not your heart be troubled: ye believe in God, believe also in me. In my Father's house are many mansions: if it were not so, I would have told you. I go to prepare a place for you.

scene.caption: A prepared place, in the Father's house
scene.alt: A golden sky over a shining city on a hill, with an open gate and a path leading toward it, and a dove flying above.

title: The Resurrection of the Body and the New Jerusalem
key_points: The believer's hope includes bodily resurrection, not merely the soul's survival.
The body is sown in corruption and weakness but raised in incorruption, glory, and power.
The dead in the Lord Jesus Christ rise first, then the living are caught up to meet Him.
God will dwell with His people in the new heaven, new earth, and the holy city, and they shall reign forever.

verse.text: So also is the resurrection of the dead. It is sown in corruption; it is raised in incorruption: It is sown in dishonour; it is raised in glory: it is sown in weakness; it is raised in power.

scene.caption: Sown in weakness, raised in glory
scene.alt: Dawn breaking over the holy city with the river of life flowing before it, an empty tomb to one side, and a trumpet sounding above.

title: Hell, Death, and the Lake of Fire
key_points: Hell (Sheol/Hades) is the holding place of the unrighteous dead, conscious and awaiting judgment.
Hell and the lake of fire are not the same; hell itself is cast into the lake of fire.
The lake of fire was prepared for the devil and his angels, not for mankind.
Free will, not cruelty, explains hell: God will not force His presence on a soul that refuses Him.

verse.text: Depart from me, ye cursed, into everlasting fire, prepared for the devil and his angels.

scene.caption: A great gulf fixed; a single light still holds
scene.alt: A dim, stormy sky over the sea with a broken chain and a small lampstand near an anchor, restrained and without any figures.

title: The Two Judgments
key_points: The judgment seat of the Lord Jesus Christ is for believers, reviewing works, not salvation.
Works are tested by fire like gold, silver, and precious stones versus wood, hay, and stubble.
Faithful believers receive crowns, which can be lost though the soul itself is kept.
At the great white throne, the books and the book of life are opened, and the deciding question is whether one's name is written there.

verse.text: Every man's work shall be made manifest: for the day shall declare it, because it shall be revealed by fire; and the fire shall try every man's work of what sort it is.

scene.caption: The books are opened; the crown is kept for the faithful
scene.alt: A great hall with pillars and light streaming down on a set of scales, with a stack of books and a crown nearby.

title: Living in the Light of Eternity
key_points: Believers lay up treasure in Heaven rather than on earth, because the heart follows the treasure.
Believers redeem the time, guard their days, and endure faithfully to the end.
Winning souls matters urgently, since every person is walking toward one of two destinations.
The hope of seeing the Lord Jesus Christ purifies the believer's life now.

verse.text: But lay up for yourselves treasures in heaven, where neither moth nor rust doth corrupt, and where thieves do not break through nor steal: For where your treasure is, there will your heart be also.

scene.caption: Treasure laid up, time redeemed, and the race endured
scene.alt: A bright day over rolling hills with a path leading forward, an hourglass and a sheaf of grain beside it, and an open Bible in the foreground.
